1.w: Now it came to pass in Iconium, according to the same, [that] they entered into the synagogue of the Jews and spoke so that a large number of both Jews and Greeks believed.

2.w: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up and poisoned the minds of the Gentiles against the brothers.

3.w: Therefore indeed they stayed a long time, speaking boldly for the Lord, testifying to the word of His grace, granting signs and wonders to be done through their hands.

4.w: Now the multitude of the city was divided, and indeed some were with the Jews, but some with the apostles.

5.w: And when there was a rush of both the Gentiles and Jews, with their rulers, to mistreat and to stone them,

6.w: having become aware, they fled to the Lycaonian cities Lystra and Derbe, and the surrounding region,

7.w: and there they continued preaching the gospel.

8.w: And in Lystra a certain man was sitting, crippled in the feet, lame from the womb of his mother, who had never walked.

9.w: This [man] heard Paul speaking, who, having looked intently at him and having seen that he has faith to be healed,

10.w: said in a loud voice, “Stand upright on your feet!” And he sprang up and began to walk.

11.w: And the crowds, having seen what Paul had done, lifted up their voice in Lycaonian, saying, “The gods have come down to us, having become like men!”

12.w: And Barnabas they began calling Zeus; and Paul, Hermes, because he was the leading speaker.

13.w: And the priest of Zeus, being just outside the city, having brought oxen and wreaths to the gates, was desiring with the crowds to sacrifice.

14.w: But the apostles Barnabas and Paul, having heard, having torn their garments, rushed out into the crowd, crying out

15.w: and saying, “Men, why do you⁺ do these things? We also are men of like nature with you⁺, proclaiming the gospel to you⁺ to turn from these vain [things] to the living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all the things in them,

16.w: who in the generations past allowed all the nations to go their ways.

17.w: And yet He did not leave Himself without witness, doing good, giving to you⁺ rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your⁺ hearts with food and gladness.”

18.w: Even saying these things, they hardly stopped the crowds from sacrificing to them.

19.w: But Jews came from Antioch and Iconium, and having persuaded the crowds, and having stoned Paul, they dragged [him] outside the city, supposing him to have died.

20.w: But the disciples having surrounded him, having risen up, he entered into the city. And on the next day he went out with Barnabas to Derbe.

21.w: And having proclaimed the gospel to that city and having discipled many, they returned to Lystra and to Iconium and to Antioch,

22.w: strengthening the souls of the disciples, exhorting [them] to continue in the faith and that “through many tribulations it is necessary for us to enter into the kingdom of God.”

23.w: And having appointed elders for them in every church, having prayed, with fasting they committed them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.

24.w: And having passed through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia,

25.w: and having spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.

26.w: And from there they sailed to Antioch, from where they had been committed to the grace of God for the work that they had fulfilled.

27.w: And having arrived and having gathered together the church, they began declaring all that God had done with them, and that He had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.

28.w: And they remained no little time with the disciples.
